goal: After this you can declare an array of structs, fill it with a loop, print a table, search by a member, find the highest value and sort the records by one member.
warmup: The class attendance register at UMT is a table. Each row is one student with roll number, name and CGPA. One struct variable is one row. An array of structs is the whole register: row 0, row 1, row 2, and so on. To find a student you look down the roll-number column. To make a merit list you sort the rows by the CGPA column.
definition: An array of structures is an array whose elements are structs. Student list[50]; makes 50 Student records. list[i] is the whole record number i (counting from 0). list[i].name is one member of that record. Everything you learned about arrays (index from 0, loops, searching, sorting) still works. The only change is that you compare or print a member, such as list[i].cgpa.
howItWorks: Declare the struct first, then the array: Student list[N];. Fill it in one of three ways: an initializer list with one brace group per record, a loop with cin >> list[i].id >> list[i].name >> list[i].cgpa, or assignments one member at a time. Print a table with a loop and \t (tab) between the members. To search by id, loop through the records and test list[i].id == target. Keep the index of the match in a variable and start it at -1, which means not found. To find the highest CGPA, do the same as the max of an array (Week 4): assume record 0 is best, then compare list[i].cgpa with list[best].cgpa and remember the index. To sort, use bubble sort or selection sort from Week 5, but compare the member you sort by, for example list[j].cgpa < list[j + 1].cgpa. Swap the WHOLE records: Student t = list[j]; list[j] = list[j + 1]; list[j + 1] = t;. One swap moves the id, the name and the cgpa together, so the student's data never gets mixed up. That is the big win over parallel arrays. Remember: you cannot write list.name, because list is the whole array. And you cannot compare two records with < or ==, so always name the member.

worked.problem: Read the id, name and CGPA of 3 students into an array of structs and print them as a table with the headings ID, Name and CGPA.
pseudocode: DECLARE struct Student and array list[3]
FOR i = 0 to 2: PRINT prompt, READ id, name, cgpa into list[i]
FOR i = 0 to 2: PRINT id, name, cgpa of list[i]

  E --> C
  C -- No --> F[/Print heading/]
  F --> G[i = 0]
  G --> H{i < 3?}
  H -- Yes --> I[/Print list i/]

  J --> H
  H -- No --> K([End])

worked.problem: Four students are stored with an initializer list. Search for the student with id 3 and print the name, then find and print the student with the highest CGPA.
pseudocode: SET list with 4 students, target = 3, found = -1
FOR each i: IF list[i].id == target THEN found = i
IF found != -1 PRINT name ELSE PRINT Not found
FOR i = 1 to 3: IF list[i].cgpa > list[best].cgpa THEN best = i

worked.problem: Three students are stored in an array of structs. Sort them by CGPA from highest to lowest using bubble sort and print the ranked list.
pseudocode: IF list[j].cgpa < list[j+1].cgpa THEN swap the whole records
FOR i = 0 to N-1: PRINT rank, name, cgpa
worked.flowchartMermaid:
flowchart TD
  A([Start]) --> B[i = 0]
  B --> C{i < N - 1?}
  C -- Yes --> D[j = 0]
  D --> E{j < N - 1 - i?}
  E -- Yes --> F{list j cgpa < list j+1 cgpa?}
  F -- Yes --> G[Swap records j and j+1]
  F -- No --> H[j = j + 1]
  G --> H
  H --> E
  E -- No --> I[i = i + 1]
  I --> C
  C -- No --> J[/Print ranked list/]
  J --> K([End])

mistakes.error: g++ reports: request for member 'name' in 'list', which is of non-class type 'Student [3]'. The array has no members; each element does.
g++ reports: no match for 'operator>' (operand types are 'Student' and 'Student'). Compare one member.
No compiler error. Reading past the end of the array is undefined behavior and may crash or corrupt data.

mistakes.wrong:
// sorting by cgpa but swapping only that member
swap(list[j].cgpa, list[j + 1].cgpa);
mistakes.error: No compiler error. The CGPAs move but the names and ids stay behind, so every student gets the wrong CGPA. Swap whole records.

examTips: list[i] is a whole record; list[i].member is one value. Write index first, then the dot.
To sort or search by a member, compare that member only; swap the whole record using a Student temporary.
Initializer list for an array of structs: one inner brace for each record.
Start a search index at -1 so you can tell 'not found' from a real index.
Loop bounds: i < N, never i <= N.

quiz.prompt: How do you print the name of record i?
quiz.explanation: list[i] picks the record and .name picks the member.

quiz.prompt: When sorting records by cgpa, what should be swapped?
quiz.hint: Keep id, name and cgpa together.
quiz.explanation: Swapping whole records keeps each student's data together.
